_meta: One bright, saturated HDR pixel in linear light, used to show that a tone-mapping curve (which compresses an unbounded high-dynamic-range value into the displayable 0..1 range) must be applied to the pixel's luminance and used to scale the color, not applied independently to each of the R, G, B channels -- because a nonlinear compression curve squeezes a large channel proportionally harder than a small one, which pulls the three channels closer together and desaturates the color, washing bright saturated highlights toward white. The pixel is [2.0, 1.2, 0.5] in linear RGB: values above 1.0 are legal in HDR and must be brought into range for a display. The Reinhard operator x -> x/(1+x) is the tone curve. Applied per channel it maps each of 2.0, 1.2, 0.5 separately, so the ratios between them shift and the saturation collapses. Applied to luminance, the curve maps the single luminance value, and the color is scaled by the ratio (mapped_luminance / luminance), which preserves the R:G:B ratios exactly -- same hue, same saturation -- while still compressing the brightness by the intended amount. luminance_weights are the Rec.709 coefficients for perceived brightness; pixel is the HDR linear color. The two tone-mapped results, their luminances, and their saturations are computed.
